question: Can one fixed encoder/decoder use visible attachments to follow a changed pair and send just one bit when its downstream reader permits that?
inputs: Four unary rule tables on a binary distinction, raw source names and two downstream attachments, two public potential query masks, actual choice of query after transmission.
forbidden_inputs: Preselected or sorted pair of rule values, pair ID, consumer ID, correct width, intersection labels, held-out accuracy during training, world-dependent width, decoder access to rules, wiring, menu, scratch, timing or actual query before transmission.
mapping: Fit shared elementary Boolean programs from downstream answers. One tied scan update, one optional one-bit readout, one pre-data width controller, and one frozen payload/query decoder across every episode. Exact finite empirical program selection. No external model service.
primary_observable: Every downstream answer and actual width, stratified by withheld pairs, worlds and reader menus; matched rewires that require a change, renamings, record-order changes, and frozen-parameter digests.
comparators_or_controls: Always two, at most one, static or stale wiring, same-world rewires, semantic width lower bound, attainable reference and independent execution.
resource_budget: One deterministic fit and bounded exhaustive evaluation as specified in the design.
first_executable_signal: Fixed rule values can require opposite answers after the two reader endpoints are rewired. An actually one-bit packet cannot distinguish four possible future answer pairs.
stop_rule: Report all cells including overfit widths or wiring failures. Any follow-up after inspection needs a separate exploratory identity.
nonclaims: Experimenter supplies truth-table rule inputs, primitive endpoint equality, shared sequential visit order, two accumulator lanes and a cost for transmitted bits. Finite transfer is specific to the disclosed reader family.
